text.p: CastleInternational Asset Management(CAM), formed last year by a 14-strong rebel team from Dunedin fund managers, has recorded its first $2bn of funds within 12 months of trading.
PNC Corporation of Philadelphia owns 80 percent of the Edinburgh-based fund manager, whose original business plan forecast around $800m of business by end of year two.
CastleInternational began trading on March 13, 1996. It was given an early boost by being chosen to handle PNC's $1.2bn mutual fund.
Now, it has picked up two new US clients: the Branch Banking and Trust Company of North Carolina ($40m), and an as yet undisclosed state fund worth $160m, concentrating on an emerging market mandate.
The fund manager was set up by Doug Waggoner, Dunedin's former marketing director in Chicago, who resigned in the summer of 1995.
It was joined by a dozen other employees of the fund manager, as Edinburgh Fund Managers picked up Dunedin for 83.25 million stg from 50.5 percent stakeholders British Linen Bank in February, 1996.

Anderson said he expects to add several hundred million dollars' worth of new clients to his portfolio in the coming months. "The new business is a great way to mark our first year. Our rate of activity is very good," he said.
"The bigger of the two new clients is very significant for us because it is a state fund," he added. "It calls upon us to demonstrate our capabilities to a particular mandate."
CastleInternational recently took on two more ex-Dunedin staff, one in its Chicago office the other in Edinburgh.
